clue.text: Elf's conceivably sober

parts.note: the word elfs is what you get when the four letters of self are made to fall into a new order, i.e. disciplined; conceivably flags the wordplay reading

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek remark that an elf might plausibly be a teetotal sort.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, SELF with DISCIPLINED as its anagram signal, and the result is ELFS, the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with strong control over their own impulses is restrained and level-headed, hence sober.

clue.text: Group with sad record

parts.note: a set is a group of things that belong together
feeling down means feeling sad

explanation.surface: A band's gloomy album, or a group linked to a miserable recording.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in writing for the record is to note it, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Sleuth's confused, being most dense

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their proper order, so the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective is baffled, so must be the dimmest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most dense' tempts as dim-witted, matching the bewildered sleuth, but it means thickest in growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush vegetation grows thickly, so the superlative describes the thickest, most luxuriant growth.

clue.text: The sure thing?

parts.note: definite means certain, sure
an article is an object or item, a thing

explanation.surface: A query about a racing cert, the sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like a mere opener but is the definition: grammarians name the word this way.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is classed as the definite article, distinguished from the indefinite 'a'.

clue.text: Suspect BBC's real game

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious and not genuine, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doubting whether the broadcaster's genuine sporting coverage is real.
explanation.definitionFit: This board game has players build words from lettered tiles, a specific example of a game.

clue.text: One gets stuck in, reaching a peak

definitions.text: One gets stuck in, reaching a peak

parts.words: One gets stuck in, reaching a peak
parts.note: a climber's tool is driven into ice and snow on the way up a mountain summit

explanation.surface: Someone who works hard and gets to the top of their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets stuck in' reads as the idiom for working with gusto; literally the tool is jabbed into the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers drive this pick into frozen slopes for grip while ascending towards a summit.

clue.text: Artist making idol in advance or newly modelled?

indicators.note: something newly modelled has been shaped afresh, so these letters are reformed in a new order

explanation.surface: An artist sculpting an idol ahead of time, or freshly modelling one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance polymath painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, so he is a famous artist.

clue.text: Young knight with a bouquet

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
a wine's bouquet is its scent

explanation.surface: A youthful knight carrying a bunch of flowers, perhaps to woo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers but here means an aroma, as of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just coming into being is in its early, immature stage, like the young.

clue.text: Melancholy broadcast praised

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A sad song that was played on air and commended.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name a state of deep gloom and hopelessness, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Commission supporting church services working group

parts.note: a commission is a task one has been given
to be for something is to support it
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A committee set up to back the church's worship arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Services' looks like church worship, but in the definition it means the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit assembled for one specific operation is a working group of the armed forces.

clue.text: Nothing the same — it must be spring

parts.note: O, the zero shape, stands for nothing
'as is' means in the same state, unchanged

explanation.surface: Since nothing changes, it must be springtime again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season; it is a water source in a desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert exists because a spring or well supplies water there.

clue.text: Wreck of canoe found in this?

definitions.text: Wreck of canoe found in this?

indicators.note: wrecking something smashes it apart, so the letters of canoe are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Where might the remains of a sunken canoe be found?
explanation.definitionFit: The open sea is where a lost vessel's remains would plausibly end up lying.

clue.text: One's distinctly square and ready to snap

definitions.text: One's distinctly square and ready to snap

parts.words: One's distinctly square and ready to snap
parts.note: an early simple photographic device was literally box-shaped and was used to take snaps

explanation.surface: A very old-fashioned person who is short-tempered and irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' and 'snap' paint a stuffy, testy person; literally they mean cube-shaped and taking photos.
explanation.definitionFit: This simple early camera was a plain cuboid case used for casual snapshots.

clue.text: You're welcome … never!

definitions.meaning: a polite reply to thanks, meaning no trouble
an emphatic denial, in no way whatsoever

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase serves both as a courteous response to thanks and as a flat refusal or denial.

clue.text: Exec on newspaper in flux, heading to the left or to the right

indicators.note: says the following little word or sits on the right of the reversed piece
in an across clue, heading leftwards means the letters of the flowing word are read backwards

parts.note: a flux is a flow, as of the tide
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper executive whose policy keeps lurching left or right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading to the left or to the right' looks political: 'heading to the left' reverses the flux word, and 'to the right' sets 'or' after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior journalist in charge of a paper's content is its top executive.

clue.text: Abandoned action to limit very French uprising

indicators.note: to limit something is to bound it on both sides, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: tres is French for very

explanation.surface: A campaign abandoned in an effort to contain a French revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' reads upward in this down clue, giving SERT, and 'to limit' has the action word enclose it. 'Very French' is the usual French-word device.
explanation.definitionFit: A place left empty and forsaken by everyone is abandoned, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Delicacy of candelabra I vacuumed round

indicators.note: turning round means the concealed run is read backwards
letters taken out of a run of words, so the piece is concealed within them

explanation.surface: A treat I sucked up from around the candelabra while cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' reverses the letters RAIVAC, found inside 'candelabra I vacuumed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeon roe is a costly luxury food, a classic example of a gourmet delicacy.

clue.text: Cook's endless hostility over one's fast

indicators.note: losing its end, the word's final letter is dropped

parts.note: a chef is a cook

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word over turns it upside down, reversing its letters

parts.note: hate is hostility

explanation.surface: A chef's never-ending animosity because someone is fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as abstaining from food; here it means quick. 'Over' gives ETAH from HATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat is the swiftest land animal, so it is one that is fast.

clue.text: Country doctor that's injected one guy from the south

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming from the south means reading upward, backwards

parts.note: a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A rural GP who has given a jab to a fellow from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country doctor' looks like a phrase but 'Country' is the definition; 'from the south' gives NAM.
explanation.definitionFit: This southeast Asian nation, capital Hanoi, is a country.

clue.text: Resort had ample illumination

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, putting these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A seaside resort had plenty of lights, like Blackpool's illuminations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' reads as a holiday town; as 're-sort' it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle's front lamp provides light on the road, a source of illumination.

clue.text: Aboard boat, couple run to see landscape?

indicators.note: being aboard means inside a vessel, so the pieces go inside the boat word

parts.note: Noah's ark was a boat
a couple is two
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Two passengers on a boat dash off to view the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landscape' seems to be the scenery to be viewed; it is an example of a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted landscape is one example of a work of art, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Don't cover up a letter that was held by 6 Down?

indicators.note: not covering means leaving exposed what sits inside the phrase, so the run of letters within it is revealed

explanation.surface: Advice not to conceal a letter, with an aside about Leonardo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't cover up' reads as don't hide; actually 'Don't cover' strips the ends of 'up a letter'. 6 Down is Leonardo da Vinci.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter holds a board for mixing colours, so Leonardo would have held one.

clue.text: Somewhere in South America, got eaten by snake

indicators.note: being eaten puts one piece inside the eater

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: Somewhere in South America a creature got swallowed by a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Colombia is a place on that continent.

clue.text: Conductor making return went by bus?

parts.note: voters return a candidate to parliament, i.e. elect them
to ride a bus is to travel on it, so rode means went by bus

explanation.surface: A bus conductor coming home on the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' and 'bus' suggest a ticket collector; it is an electrical conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: This terminal passes electric current into or out of a medium, so it conducts electricity.

clue.text: Essential oil container, perhaps holding essence of mustard

indicators.note: holding means enclosing, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle, which might hold oil

indicators.note: the essence is the heart, so the middle letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An essential oil bottle containing extract of mustard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential oil' reads as a phrase, but 'Essential' is the definition; T is the central letter of MUSTARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absolutely necessary is crucial or indispensable, the same sense.

clue.text: Thorn witch cut occasionally as stimulant

indicators.note: cutting letters at intervals keeps only every other one

explanation.surface: A witch trims a thornbush now and then to make a potion.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink or medicine that invigorates and restores energy is a pick-me-up, a stimulant.

clue.text: Unqualified batsman's fate in both innings?

definitions.meaning: in a two-innings cricket match a batsman dismissed each time is out and then out again

explanation.walkthrough: A cricket match can give each side two innings, so a batsman can be dismissed twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means total or utter, as in an unqualified rogue, without any reservation.

clue.text: Red Cross?

parts.note: red means communist, and the communist emblem shows two tools crossed over each other

explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Cross' looks like the aid organisation; 'Red' is communist and the cross is two crossed tools.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet emblem shows a mallet and a curved blade crossed, a communist symbol.
